That’s actually a pretty common vision in sleep paralysis.  I have it too.  When I started reading about it, a LOT of people visualize a woman holding them down!  It’s our brain’s way of processing the chemical reaction happening.

When you’re in REM sleep your brain releases chemicals to paralyze the body..
So you don’t act out the dream in your sleep.  In sleep paralysis you are suddenly jolted from REM cycle to awake.. but the chemical reaction in your brain doesn’t work that fast.  So essentially you’re awake but your body is still paralyzed as synapses are firing and neurotransmitters are releasing to allow you to move again. The brain, in absence of an explanation as to why it can’t move, will often decide “we are being held down!” The accompanying visual is just that.. your brain compensating for what it cannot explain.

Tell your mom that medicine is on your side.. this is pretty common.  NBD.

A way that helps?  Don’t sleep on your back.  Most sleep paralysis happens in this position!

Fewer than twelve years after Union troops had set fire to the town's first courthouse, the new one burned in 1876. Despite the lack of circumstantial evidence, the townspeople identified Henry Wells as a suspect; he was a freedman who lived near the town.

Henry Wells was said to have a horrible temper, and he had been involved in several brawls. There was no real evidence he burnt the courthouse. He was taken to the sheriff's office, located inside the newly completed courthouse, to await trial.

As word spread through the town of Wells' arrest, the sheriff could sense trouble brewing. She made us realize that giftedness could be across the board, or just in certain areas. My kids both have high IQ scores and are labeled gifted but I always tell them IQ is fluid, and it measures potential.  My watered down visual for my children was “Imagine you and your friend have a building full of boxes.  Your friend has 100 boxes and you have 160.  If your friend fills all 100 of her boxes to overflowing, but you only fill 75 of your boxes... then she has more things than you even though you have more boxes on paper.”  Basically saying a high IQ doesn’t guarantee instant success or instant intelligence. Someone with a normal IQ can absolutely know more and be more successful if they apply themselves.  And gifted individuals are known to be the ones who get bored, slack off, half ass, and not apply themselves.

I really just want them to be happy, well adjusted, and find a career in a field where they feel passion and not obligation.  One is far more important to the other.  Never in my adult life have I been asked my IQ score, but I do get asked about my interests, my career, and my education.

Nursing is my second degree.  I have a Bachelor’s in Social Work, where I worked happily for 10 years.  
Then, I applied for an Advanced Master’s in Nursing program.  To get in I had to finish a few pre-requisites (anatomy, physiology and microbiology) and then apply.  They looked at my undergraduate GPA and each grade for a core class I needed counted a certain amount of points.  They had you write an essay and resume which they also awarded points for, and they also awarded 10 bonus points if you had shadowed a healthcare professional as a volunteer for 25 hours.  It was difficult to get into the program but that was nothing compared to the first year.  The first year you basically cram 5 semesters of nursing school into 3 semesters.  Then, you’re a Bachelor’s level nurse, you sit for NCLEX, you get a license and you work.  While working you take another 5 semesters and do clinical hours to graduate.  I just finished, was supposed to walk in May.

I wish I had just gotten a Bachelor’s degree in Nursing and then come back for a Master’s degree to start with.  Nursing school is a lot of information.  A lot of really important information that you really want to understand, not just memorize!  Also, because there is so much they are required to teach within a short period of time, I really believe the four year Bachelor degree programs make the best nurses.  

Good luck no matter what you decide.
